title: Monotonicity conjecture for the normalized elliptic-integral approximation error
statement:
Let $\mathscr{K}(r)$ be the complete elliptic integral of the first kind, let

$$
G(r)=\frac{\log(2\mathscr{K}(r)/\pi)}{\log((\operatorname{arth} r)/r)},
$$

and define

$$
f(r)=\frac{1}{r^2}\left[G(r)-\frac34\right],\qquad r\in(0,1).
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture for $f$.** The function $f$ is strictly increasing from $(0,1)$ onto $(1/320,1/4)$.

If true, this would identify the sharp constants in the refined two-sided approximation with exponents $3/4+\alpha r^2$ and $3/4+\beta r^2$. The statement is presented as a conjecture based on earlier bounds and computation; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04072

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).
source_name: Song-Liang Qiu, Qi Bao, Xiao-Yan Ma and Hong-Biao Jiang, “On a Conjecture Concerning the Approximates of Complete Elliptic Integral of the First Kind by Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent”, arXiv:2103.04072 (2021).
